title: Distribution-Free Prediction Sets for Two-Layer Hierarchical Models
journal_or_venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

content.abstract_summary: Develops distribution-free conformal prediction sets for clustered and hierarchical data structures where observations within a cluster (e.g. repeated PK measures from the same patient) are dependent, but clusters are exchangeable. Provides valid finite-sample coverage at both cluster and unit levels.
key_findings: Standard split conformal fails on clustered data due to intra-cluster correlation
Proposes cluster-level split conformal and leave-one-cluster-out methods that maintain valid nominal coverage
Establishes theoretical guarantees for both new cluster prediction and unit-level prediction within observed clusters
Directly applicable to hierarchical clinical trial data with repeated sampling per subject
limitations: Requires exchangeability at the cluster level (patients must be exchangeable even if repeated samples are correlated)
Conservative prediction intervals if number of clusters is small (<20)

extracted_claims.text: When data are clustered, standard exchangeability is violated. We develop methods that provide exact finite-sample coverage guarantees by leveraging cluster-level exchangeability.

gaps_addressed: Provides exact mathematical formulation for applying conformal prediction to repeated-measures PK/PD trial data in Pillar 2 (M2.2)

provenance.notes: Added 2026-08-29 by Antigravity review. Key reference for hierarchical/clustered conformal prediction in PK/PD.
